# Pengcheng Huang (黄鹏程)

> Pengcheng Huang is a Ph.D. student in Computer Science at Northeastern University (China), advised by Prof. Zhenghao Liu, working on large language models (LLMs), foundation models, and LLM agents. M.S. (advisor: Prof. Tong Xiao) and B.S. also from Northeastern University. Since 2025.03: visiting Ph.D. student at THUNLP (Tsinghua University) and intern at ModelBest, working on general agentic capabilities of foundation models.

Several researchers share the name Pengcheng Huang. This one is the NLP / LLM researcher at Northeastern University (China): GitHub `passionate11`, Google Scholar `VA9mUOsAAAAJ`, ORCID `0009-0006-1236-5500`, DBLP `129/2239-4`, OpenReview `~Pengcheng_Huang3`. Contact: pengcheng.neu@outlook.com

## First-author papers (with project pages)

- [EC²-Bench (EC2-Bench): Empowering Edge Agents: A Systematic Analysis of Edge-Cloud Collaboration in LLM Agent Execution (arXiv 2026)](https://passionate11.github.io/ec2-bench-project-page/): EC2-Bench is a benchmark for edge-cloud collaboration in long-horizon LLM agents, jointly measuring task performance, resource usage and privacy exposure. 128 executable digital-workspace tasks (100 with privacy annotations) on the OpenClaw agent harness, comparing query routing, per-step routing, edge-controlled delegation and edge-controlled advisory across edge models of increasing capability. [arXiv:2610.17816](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17816) · [Code](https://github.com/OpenBMB/EC2-Bench) · [Dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/chengpingan/EC2-Bench)
- [UNCODE: Empirical Analysis of Decoding Biases in Masked Diffusion Models (ACL 2026, oral)](https://passionate11.github.io/Uncode-project-page/): shows that uncertainty-based decoding in masked diffusion LLMs (LLaDA, Dream) suffers a rigid boundary bias and a trivial token bias, and proposes UNCODE, a training-free unmasking calibration with a positional trajectory prior and a semantic informativeness prior; more than 7% better than existing decoding strategies across 3 MDMs and 7 benchmarks. Earlier arXiv title: "PC-Sampler: Position-Aware Calibration of Decoding Bias in Masked Diffusion Models". [ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.311/) · [arXiv:2508.13021](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.13021) · [Code](https://github.com/NEUIR/Uncode)
- [ParamMute: Suppressing Knowledge-Critical FFNs for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation (NeurIPS 2025)](https://passionate11.github.io/ParamMute-project-page/): finds that unfaithful RAG answers coincide with over-activated mid-to-deep FFN layers (UA-FFNs), suppresses them and adds a knowledge-preference adaptation module; introduces the CoFaithfulQA benchmark of natural knowledge conflicts. Earlier arXiv title: "PIP-KAG: Mitigating Knowledge Conflicts in Knowledge-Augmented Generation via Parametric Pruning". [OpenReview](https://openreview.net/forum?id=CyUq9D99vE) · [arXiv:2502.15543](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.15543) · [Code](https://github.com/OpenBMB/ParamMute)
- [Translate-and-Revise: Boosting Large Language Models for Constrained Translation (CCL 2024)](https://passionate11.github.io/Translate-and-Revise-project-page/): TAR, a training-free prompting method in which an LLM translates with constraints, is told which constraints it missed, and revises its translation; about 15% higher constraint accuracy than standard LLM translation across four constrained translation tasks. [ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2024.ccl-1.82/) · [arXiv:2407.13164](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.13164)
